clue.text: Almost put out of service for protest

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to demob is to release from military service

explanation.surface: A machine nearly taken out of service, perhaps as a gesture of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: Demob (short for demobilise) loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is the everyday short form of demonstration, a public protest march or rally.

clue.text: Reflecting sound selection after last goes top

indicators.note: the final letter moves up to the front, which is the top of a down entry

blocks.note: a selection is a choice

explanation.surface: Someone weighing a choice of sound recordings after the last one is put at the top of the list.
explanation.walkthrough: The E at the end of CHOICE moves to the front to give ECHOIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoic describes something that imitates or echoes a sound, as onomatopoeic words do.

clue.text: Prevent large amount of money being raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: pots of money means a great deal of it

explanation.surface: Someone trying to block a big sum of money from being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to prevent it from happening; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Run miles over a very long time

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another means it comes first

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for miles
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A runner covering many miles over a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks athletic, sitting next to miles, but it means to be in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to manage it; both verbs mean to be in control of.

clue.text: Difference in new paintings going up in price

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top
the pieces before this word are placed inside the word after it

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
paintings are art
a price is a cost

explanation.surface: An art dealer noting the gap between new paintings and older ones as prices rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' only applies to the paintings, since this is a down entry; 'new' stays as it is and sits before them.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrast is a striking dissimilarity, so the noun is a synonym of difference.

clue.text: Man's crisis misrepresented as problem with ego

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are presented in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's mid-life crisis wrongly portrayed as nothing more than an inflated ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissism is excessive self-love, an overblown ego; the name comes from Narcissus, who fell for his own reflection.

clue.text: Liking quiet entrance

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
read as the verb en-TRANCE, to delight or bewitch

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a discreet doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun for a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to put under a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness or taste for something, so it is a noun synonym of liking.

clue.text: JFK, for instance, as screened in fair portrayal

indicators.note: something screened inside the following words is concealed within them, running across their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: A film about President Kennedy, judged as a fair portrayal of him.
explanation.walkthrough: JFK looks like the president, but it is also the code for New York's John F Kennedy airport.
explanation.definitionFit: John F Kennedy International is New York's main airport, so JFK is an example of one.

clue.text: Assertion I, for one, heard

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the phrase sounds when spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: the letter I is an example of a vowel

explanation.surface: Someone making a claim and saying they, personally, have heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the letter, one of the vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or statement, so it is a synonym of assertion.

clue.text: Paint line and circle in reduced playing area

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
the earlier pieces go inside the shortened word that follows

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
the letter O is circle-shaped
a court is where tennis or basketball is played

explanation.surface: Instructions for painting the lines and centre circle on a smaller pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: COURT is cut to COUR, and L and O go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour is paint or pigment, as in a tube of colour; the noun stands for paint.

clue.text: Fee includes something done in medical business

indicators.note: one word includes another by holding it inside itself

blocks.note: a fee is a price
an act is a deed, something done

explanation.surface: A clinic's bill including a charge for the procedure carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's or dentist's practice is their professional business, so the noun fits a medical firm.

clue.text: Speculator is improperly securing me three valuable commodities

definitions.note: names the class through its three best-known members, gold, silver and platinum

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the following word is held within the earlier ones
done improperly means done wrongly, so the letters end up out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An investor confesses to having wrongly locked the speaker into three valuable assets.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of 'Speculator is' plus 'me' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold, silver and platinum are the familiar precious metals, rare and valuable commodities traded on markets.

clue.text: Telling act that follows political no-win situation

definitions.text: act that follows political no-win situation

blocks.note: first meaning: narrating, giving an account

blocks.clueFragment: act that follows political no-win situation
blocks.note: second meaning: counting the votes again after a tied or too-close election

explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling' looks like an adjective meaning revealing; it is the verb form, narrating. The second part plays on RE-COUNTING after an election where nobody has won.
explanation.definitionFit: Recounting is narrating a story, and also counting ballots again after an indecisive result.

clue.text: Piece of wheel, it's said

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the rods joining a wheel's hub to its rim
second meaning: talked, past tense of speak

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like a signal that the word sounds like another; here it simply supplies the second meaning, the past tense of speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoke is a bar radiating from a wheel hub, and spoke is also the past tense of speak, meaning said.

clue.text: Some land in Mediterranean port

blocks.note: first meaning: a unit of land area
second meaning: ..., the ancient port city in northern Israel

explanation.walkthrough: Acre is a historic port on the Bay of Haifa, famous from the Crusades.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measure of land area, and Acre is also a coastal city on Israel's Mediterranean shore.

clue.text: Iron, carbon, and chromium, for example, workers put in sort of steel

definitions.text: Iron, carbon, and chromium, for example

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the word's letters are reshaped
one piece is put inside another, which then surrounds it

blocks.note: workers are men, as in a gang of workmen
the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers adding iron, carbon and chromium to make a particular grade of steel, as stainless steel is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' looks like part of the definition's metallurgy, but it is only raw letters to be reshaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, carbon and chromium are all chemical elements, so they are examples of the class.

clue.text: Fish from middle of jetty beside Waterloo

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its single central letter
beside means placed next to, so one piece directly precedes the other

blocks.note: the central letter of the word
Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo was a rout

explanation.surface: Someone fishing from a pier next to Waterloo, perhaps on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo looks like a London place; here it is the battle, a crushing defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a common freshwater game fish, so the answer is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Holidaymaker runs into popular person in bar?

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, which then surrounds it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
someone who leaves generous gratuities is well liked by bar staff

explanation.surface: A tourist dashing into a pub where a popular character is drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful description: bar staff like a customer who tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is someone on a short holiday or day out, a British word for a tourist.

clue.text: Heads off to regatta in magnificent condition for sailing

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, and 'off' stands in for 'of'

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Crews heading off to a regatta with their boats in superb shape for racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' reads as setting out, but it means the first letters of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat in good trim is balanced and ready to sail, so trim is its sailing condition.

clue.text: Labour didn't produce such funding

blocks.note: surface reading: money the Labour Party failed to raise
setter's reading: money that arrives without anyone working for it, such as dividends or rent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' with a capital looks like the British political party, but it means work; the capital is just the start of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Income from investments, interest or rent, rather than wages for work, is termed unearned in tax language.

clue.text: Cure part of extreme dyslexia

indicators.note: part of the following words means a run of consecutive letters lifted from inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone seeking treatment for one element of a severe reading difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, so the noun is a synonym of cure.

clue.text: Bottle child found under vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece found under another comes after it

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a boy is a child

explanation.surface: A bottle, or a child, discovered beneath a parked car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large rounded bottle, often in a protective frame, used for acids or home brewing.

clue.text: Decoration for room shows ship crossing river

indicators.note: the vessel crosses the river by spanning it, so it surrounds that letter

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a steamer is a steamship

explanation.surface: A cabin decoration depicting a boat crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamers are long paper ribbons hung up as party decorations in a room.

clue.text: Pile of hay that Pat has discarded

indicators.note: what has been discarded is thrown away, so those letters leave the full name

blocks.note: Pat is a short form of the name Patrick

explanation.surface: A haystack that a farmhand called Pat has left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick, whose nickname is Pat, discards PAT from his full name to leave RICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a large stack of hay or straw, often thatched, built in a field.

clue.text: As such, including university study

indicators.note: one piece includes the other by holding it inside itself

blocks.note: per se is Latin for in itself, or as such
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: University study, considered for its own sake.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully, so it is a verb synonym of study.

clue.text: Top performer that represents state in standard array

definitions.text: that represents state in standard array

blocks.note: first meaning: a leading actor or celebrity

blocks.clueFragment: that represents state in standard array
blocks.note: second meaning: one of the fifty emblems on the US flag, one for each state

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning usual; it is a noun meaning flag, and the Stars and Stripes carries one emblem per state.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a leading performer, and each star on the American flag stands for one state.

clue.text: One tune I'd rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a different order, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician confessing they rearranged a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a number, but it is the adjective, as in being of one mind.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are united act as one, joined together in a single body or purpose.

clue.text: Man in charge of section of the body

blocks.note: first meaning: the army NCO who commands a section of soldiers
second meaning: bodily, physical

explanation.walkthrough: 'Section of the body' reads as one phrase about anatomy, but it splits after 'section'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer leading a section, and corporal also means bodily, as in corporal punishment.
